exact_capability_hypothesis.implementation: The installed LuaJIT integrated C API sampler, controlled via luaJIT_profile_start/stop with luaJIT_profile_dumpstack in a C-only callback; NOT FProfiler or public jit.profile. A compatible native adapter is not currently available/verified.
exact_capability_hypothesis.mechanism: Inference: direct LuaJIT stack dumping on callback-supplied lua_State with bounded native buffering could name currently executing Lua work without per-method wrappers or GLua callbacks. No guarantee of safe GMod embedding or usable observer effect.
exact_capability_hypothesis.difference_from_closed_work: New direct evidence of implemented installed native exports; uses no public Lua profile module, wrapper calls or external OS instruction-pointer-to-Lua symbol project.
exact_capability_hypothesis.jit: Upstream supports interpreted and compiled Lua. Function/line modes flush traces at start and stop, so later comparisons must warm both relevant states outside capture. Inlining prevents simple one-to-one line attribution.
exact_capability_hypothesis.yield_and_wait: Only the callback-supplied active state may be inspected. Do not time an entire coroutine lifetime or charge paused yields. Windows timer samples elapsed intervals; delayed C/host samples can carry earlier VMstate with a later stack. Keep VMstate separate and do not call this exclusive CPU.
exact_capability_hypothesis.realm: Underlying sampler has one global instance; profile server realm alone in listen-host process, not client and server concurrently.
exact_capability_hypothesis.embedding: Facepunch issue3203 documents CLuaInterface wrong-state danger when invoking GLua C functions from Lua callbacks. Avoiding that interface is a rationale for C-only callback, not proof of safety.
exact_capability_hypothesis.callback_cost: Upstream dumpstack itself can format/grow its internal string buffer; bounded adapter storage does not make sampling allocation-free or overhead-free.
